key_insight: MedHarnessBench shows that healthcare-specific runtime support can improve both task success and the quality of agent actions, not just final outcomes.
clinical_relevance: For healthcare AI systems, this benchmark helps distinguish whether failures come from the model, the tool/workflow harness, or their interaction, which is critical for safer deployment.
method: Defined the Medical Harness Protocol to separately score seven process dimensions in healthcare agent execution.
Built MedHarnessBench with 342 executable tasks spanning FHIR/EHR operations, admin interfaces, and multimodal clinical tools.
Tracked intervention traces to see whether runtime support was available, used, and carried into later behavior.
evidence_signal: The authors report more than 16,000 controlled task executions, with MedHarness improving terminal success, intermediate completion, and healthcare-specific process quality.
watch_item: Results come from benchmarked, controlled workflows, so real-world performance may differ when systems face messy clinical data, changing policies, or high-stakes edge cases.
paper_title: MedHarnessBench: A Unified Benchmark for Healthcare Agent Evaluation
